findings.title: Equity as the manner of witnessing
findings.claim: The preposition bi makes equity the manner or instrument through which witnessing is performed.
findings.mechanism: Bi attaches the witness role to al-qist, so testimony is enacted through an equity standard rather than merely being about fairness.
findings.reader_payoff: Fairness becomes the method of testimony, not only its subject.
findings.containment: The ordinary command to bear equitable witness remains primary; this finding adds the local instrumental relation and no external setting.

epistemic.reason: Trusted word-analysis and QAC evidence directly supply the preposition's local grammatical function.

findings.title: A measured equity standard
findings.claim: Al-qist names a definite, measurable equity standard, distinct in wording from the later command to act justly.
findings.mechanism: The definite noun under bi supplies the standard for testimony, while the later ta'dilu and i'dilu forms supply repeated justice actions; the ayah therefore joins measured standard and enacted balance.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel justice as a concrete measure before hearing it as a command.
findings.containment: The primary meaning remains equitable testimony; the measured-share pressure is bounded to this focus wording and does not import an unprovided scene.

epistemic.reason: The local noun and later focus forms are securely supplied, while the broader lexical pressure is retained only in the bounded relation stated here.

findings.title: One justice program
findings.claim: The conjunction wa keeps the hostility prohibition within the same justice program introduced by the witness command.
findings.mechanism: It coordinates the first command sequence with the ban on hatred-driven injustice, making the second instruction a continuation rather than a detached topic.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning about bias remains connected to the duty of witnessing fairly.
findings.containment: The finding concerns the local coordination of clauses and does not infer a wider discourse structure.

epistemic.reason: The supplied conjunction and trusted grammatical analysis directly support the coordination.

findings.title: A prohibition over the causal verb
findings.claim: La places a prohibition over the emphatic imperfect and blocks the pathway from hostility to injustice.
findings.mechanism: The particle scopes over yajrimannakum, framing the following causal movement as a prohibited outcome rather than a bare description.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears a stop placed before bias can become conduct.
findings.containment: The finding preserves the ordinary prohibition and adds its scope; it does not claim that the feeling itself is grammatically erased.

epistemic.reason: The focus QAC parse and trusted word-analysis record directly specify the prohibitive scope.

findings.title: Hostility as pressure into wrong
findings.claim: Yajrimannakum depicts hostility as capable of driving the believers into injustice and making them bear culpable wrong.
findings.mechanism: The emphatic imperfect and second-person object suffix assign agent-like pressure to the hostility, the believers as affected objects, and non-justice as the resulting conduct.
findings.reader_payoff: The danger is internal: a feeling can recruit the addressed community into an unjust act.
findings.containment: The canonical warning remains intact; the finding describes the supplied causal grammar and does not claim that every possible root association is active.

epistemic.reason: The causal grammatical relation is directly anchored, while the culpability pressure is kept within the supplied local lexical boundary.

findings.title: Hatred as the grammatical driver
findings.claim: Shana'an is made the grammatical driver of the justice failure, so deep animus supplies the active pressure rather than the opposing people.
findings.mechanism: The verbal noun stands as the nominative subject before the impelling verb, locating causation in hostile aversion and leaving the group as its object of hostility.
findings.reader_payoff: The sentence makes the inner force of hatred visible as an actor in the warning.
findings.containment: The finding concerns subject assignment and its local semantic effect; it does not deny the ordinary reference to a disliked group.

epistemic.reason: The subject role is directly supplied, with lexical pressure retained only as the bounded notion of hostile aversion.

findings.title: The unnamed group test
findings.claim: Qawmin leaves the hostile people unnamed and indefinite, so the justice test applies across group hostilities.
findings.mechanism: The indefinite genitive collective avoids binding the prohibition to one named opponent and keeps the direction of hostility open.
findings.reader_payoff: No particular disliked group can be treated as outside the rule supplied by this wording.
findings.containment: The finding stays with the indefinite form and does not identify any historical group or add a context ayah.

epistemic.reason: The QAC morphology and trusted word-analysis record directly support the indefinite collective reading.

findings.title: Pressure toward a result
findings.claim: Ala directs the warning toward a concrete result, so hatred is barred from pressing the addressees into failing justice.
findings.mechanism: The preposition governs the subordinate outcome clause and links the affective pressure to the conduct it must not produce.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning concerns what hatred can make happen, not only what it feels like.
findings.containment: The ordinary ban on injustice remains primary; the result-oriented pressure is a local grammatical effect.

epistemic.reason: The supplied preposition and trusted analysis directly establish the result relation.

findings.title: The compressed forbidden result
findings.claim: Alla compresses subordination and negation into the single forbidden result of not acting justly.
findings.mechanism: Its fused form tightens the link between the hostility clause and the negated justice verb that follows it.
findings.reader_payoff: A whole prohibited outcome arrives in a compact grammatical unit before the command is repeated positively.

epistemic.reason: The focus morpheme split and trusted grammatical support directly establish the fused subordinate negation.

findings.title: The specific failure justice names
findings.claim: Ta'dilu names the specific subordinate failure being prevented: departure from equitable conduct.
findings.mechanism: The plural subjunctive sits inside the negated result clause, while its balance and deviation pressure shows the line hatred could bend away from justice.
findings.reader_payoff: The prohibition points to a definite behavioral failure rather than an undefined moral mood.
findings.containment: The local justice/balance reading remains primary; the deviation pressure sharpens the warning without replacing it.

findings.title: An immediate summons

findings.title: From restraint to active justice

findings.title: Custodial witness chain
findings.claim: The ayah can be read as instituting a continuing custodial office in which an upright public standard is maintained for God, expressed through knowledgeable witness, and completed in conduct answerable to penetrating knowledge.

findings.reader_payoff: Fair testimony becomes an office with a maintained standard and accountable conduct, rather than a single utterance.
findings.containment: This is an attributed focus-local HFT synthesis; the ordinary command to stand for God and testify with equity remains intact, and no wider system or untraced motive claim is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT trace supplies focus coordinates, roots, roles, and returning contacts, while the reader identity is legacy_unbound and the source packet is broader than the declared pericope.
